reviews.title: Weak privacy!
reviews.text:
Telegram has a serious doxxing and privacy problem. Its current design makes it far too easy to use OSINT techniques to connect information scattered across public groups, channels, shared links, usernames, profile photos, and other publicly accessible content. A single message containing a link can potentially become a starting point for identifying a user’s other accounts and online activity, especially when old messages remain accessible.

The problem is not simply that users share information publicly; it is that Telegram provides very few safeguards against someone systematically aggregating those fragments into a detailed profile of an individual, potentially exposing highly sensitive personal information.

For a platform that markets itself around privacy, this is unacceptable. Telegram needs stronger anti-doxxing protections, better control over the discoverability and persistence of user-generated content, and clearer privacy defaults.

reviews.text: Telegram’s system for handling phone numbers and account deletions is an absolute trainwreck. I tried changing my registered phone number to my current one, only to be blocked because the system claims the number is “already connected to an account.” This happens because phone carriers recycle numbers, and the previous owner left their account active. Instead of letting me claim my own number by verifying SMS ownership, Telegram completely freezes the process. To make matters worse, when you try to log into that recycled account to wipe it so you can actually use your own number, Telegram tries to block you with email resets or cloud passwords — and essentially pushes you to buy a Telegram Premium subscription just to bypass wait times and clear out the old account. Absolute garbage user experience. You shouldn’t have to jump through ridiculous paywalls or complex workarounds just to use your own phone number on a messaging app. Fix your account migration rules.

My account was stolen even though:
	•	The phone number and eSIM are physically mine

	•	Easy, disposable accounts
	•	Bots that look legit
	•	Stolen accounts with real names and photos used to scam friends and family

If you’re a scammer, Telegram is paradise.
If you’re a victim, you’re just background noise.

Takeaway for regular users:
	•	Don’t treat Telegram like a trustworthy backbone of your digital life
	•	Don’t rely on it as your only contact channel
